title: Woo Fung Ling

page_data.en:
Shanghai Municipal Council.

C. I. D.
I. O. REG
No. 9 S H
Date 26: 4: 16
April 26th 1916.

POLICE FORCE,
(DETECTIVE BRANCH)

Sir,
General Yang is reported to have yesterday received a letter from the rebels demanding a statement of his position in the present situation. If no reply is received drastic measures are hinted at. On receipt of the letter General Yang issued an order to the troops to take special precautions.
At 4 p.m. yesterday General Yang held a conference with his subordinates military officials at which he announced his intention to keep the peace and to take no part in the present political upheaval. He added that if any person took rash steps without consideration at present, not only would foreigners interfere but the Empire itself would be shaken to the foundations. He went on to say that Shanghai being an important commercial port was in a different position from any other place and while he did not wish to force his own personal ideas on the Peking Government he felt that peace and good order should be maintained here at all costs. He then invited the views of those present but none of them made any statements and the conference had therefore little result.
The 4th Division having been stationed at Shanghai for a considerable time, some of the officers are said to be in communication with the local rebels. This must be known to General Yang who, however, pretends that he knows nothing about it.
Yesterday General Woo Fung Ling 何豐林 in command of the troops at Sungkiang sent 4 prisoners to General Yang's yamen at Lunghwa. It is said that one of them is an officer and the other three privates who were arrested for communicating with the rebels. On the other hand it is rumoured that they are rebels. They have been sent to the Military Court for trial.
It is reported that Commander Zung of Woosung forts has received a wireless communication from a certain warship that the Cantonese have sent a cruiser to bombard the forts. The cruiser will get

1916年4月26日。

警务处，
（侦探科）

先生：
据报，杨将军昨日收到叛军来信，要求他表明在当前局势下的立场。信中暗示，若不予回复，将采取严厉措施。杨将军接到信件后，下令部队采取特别预防措施。
昨日下午4时，杨将军与其下属军官举行会议，宣布其维持和平、不参与当前政治动荡的意图。他补充说，如果目前有人不加考虑地采取鲁莽行动，不仅外国人会进行干涉，整个帝国也将根基动摇。他接着表示，上海作为重要的商业港口，地位与其他地方不同，虽然他不愿将自己的个人观点强加于北京政府，但他认为无论如何都必须在此维持和平与良好秩序。随后他征求与会者的意见，但无人发言，因此会议成果甚微。
由于第四师驻防上海已相当长一段时间，据说部分军官与当地叛军有联络。此事杨将军必然知晓，但他佯装不知。
昨日，指挥松江部队的吴凤岭将军何豐林向龙华杨将军衙门送去了四名囚犯。据说其中一人是军官，另外三人是士兵，他们因与叛军联络而被捕。另一方面，有谣言称他们是叛军。他们已被送往军事法庭受审。

of the above martial law has been proclaimed
and it is also said that mines are being laid
at night in the vicinity of the forts.
Two robbers were shot at the Arsenal yesterday.
Two car loads of ammunition was sent from
Woosung to Wusieh last night by the S.N.Railway
escorted by an officer and 17 soldiers.
At 6 p.m. last night martial law was again
proclaimed in Chapel.
Two more warships the Foh An and the Ching
Woo have arrived and are lying off the Arsenal.
Information received from Wusieh this morning
is to the effect that the outposts of the Kiangyin
rebels are at Tsingyang some twenty li away and
that the Government troops are massing with a
view to attacking them. There have been no
fighting in the Wusieh City but the opposing forces
have come into contact in the surrounding country
without either side showing any superiority.
In Wusieh people are going about their
business as usual. The soldiers who fill the
streets are well conducted and orderly.
Your Obedient Servant,
[Signature]
Chief Detective Inspector.
Captain Superintendent of Police.

以受海军部委派为借口，接近炮台。鉴于上述情况，已宣布戒严，另有消息称夜间正在炮台附近水域布设水雷。
昨日，两名劫匪在兵工厂被枪击。
昨晚，由一名军官和17名士兵护送，两车弹药经沪宁铁路从吴淞运往无锡。
昨晚6时，闸北再次宣布戒严。
另有两艘军舰“福安”号和“靖武”号抵达，停泊在兵工厂附近。
今晨从无锡收到的消息指出，江阴叛军的前哨位于二十里外的青阳（音译），政府军正在集结，准备发动攻击。无锡城内未发生战斗，但周边地区敌对势力已有接触，双方均未显示出优势。
在无锡，人们照常从事日常活动。充斥街头的士兵行为端正，秩序井然。

您顺从的仆人，
[签名]
首席侦探督察长。
警察总监。

副本已送交特别巡捕房。
